goal_text: (Reused from research_synth_019) Compare five post-hoc interpretability methods for neural networks — LIME, SHAP, Grad-CAM, Integrated Gradients, and Attention Visualization — on core mechanism, applicable model types, and one known limitation of each.
ground_truth: LIME: fits a local linear surrogate model using perturbed samples around a prediction; model-agnostic; limitation: explanations are unstable across runs due to random perturbations. SHAP: assigns Shapley values from cooperative game theory to attribute feature contributions; model-agnostic but expensive for exact computation; limitation: can be misleading when features are correlated. Grad-CAM: uses gradient of class score with respect to CNN feature maps to produce saliency maps; CNN-only; limitation: spatial resolution limited to feature map size. Integrated Gradients: integrates gradients along a path from a baseline input to the actual input; differentiable models only; limitation: choice of baseline significantly affects attribution. Attention Visualization: directly visualizes attention weight matrices in transformer models; attention-based models only; limitation: attention weights do not reliably correspond to feature importance.
